Architecture Highlights & High-Throughput Engineering

• Decoupled Ingestion & Rendering: OpenCV camera capture runs asynchronously with auto-exposure sensor locking to eliminate frame dropouts and camera buffer lag.

• In-Place NumPy Matrix Memory Re-Use: Frame transformations reuse pre-allocated ndarray memory blocks, preventing garbage collection stalls during high-rate live streaming.

• Dual Target Deployment: Local Python/Streamlit execution for intensive native laboratory defenses, supplemented by a zero-install static WebAssembly/Vision API build for browser demonstration.

03 // DIP METHODOLOGY
Digital Image Processing: Spatial & Edge Analytics
Canny Edge & Gradient Fundamentals

• Gaussian Smoothing: Convolves input image with a 2D Gaussian kernel G(x,y) to suppress high-frequency noise before derivative operators.

G(x,y) = (1 / 2πσ²) · exp(-(x² + y²) / 2σ²)

• Gradient Calculation: Computes spatial derivatives Gx and Gy via 3x3 Sobel masks to obtain gradient magnitude and angle θ.

|G| = √(Gx² + Gy²), θ = arctan(Gy / Gx)

• Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS): Thins broad gradient ridges into 1-pixel wide edge candidates by tracking directional local maxima.

• Hysteresis Thresholding: Uses dual thresholds [T_low, T_high]. Edges above T_high are certified; pixels below T_low are discarded; intermediate pixels are preserved if 8-connected.

04 // CV APPLICATIONS
Computer Vision: Real-Time Motion Detection & Tracking
Temporal Differencing & Object Localization

• Consecutive Frame Differencing: Measures instantaneous temporal intensity gradients across consecutive video frames to detect motion vectors.

ΔI_t(x,y) = |I_t(x,y) - I_{t-1}(x,y)| > θ

• Running Background Accumulation: Dynamically adapts the background reference model against ambient lighting shifts and shadow drift.

B_t = α · I_t + (1 - α) · B_{t-1}

• Morphological Filtering: Applies 5x5 structural opening (erosion followed by dilation) to suppress optical camera shot noise and sensor jitter.

• Contour Clustering & HUD: Bounding rectangles isolate active regions (Area > 1000px) and calculate real-time scene motion index percentages.

06 // MATHEMATICAL RIGOR
Mathematical Formulations & Theoretical Defense
1. 2D Spatial Convolution & Gaussian Kernel
g(x,y) = ∑∑ h(s,t) · f(x-s, y-t)

Gaussian 2D Distribution: G(x,y) = (1 / 2πσ²) exp(-(x²+y²)/2σ²)

Parameter σ defines the spatial bandwidth cutoff. Larger kernels eliminate noise while diffusing object boundaries.

2. Otsu's Bimodal Variance Maximization
σ_B²(T) = ω₀(T) · ω₁(T) · [μ₀(T) - μ₁(T)]²

Between-Class Separation: Maximizes statistical separability between foreground and background intensity classes across all possible 256 gray levels.

Completely nonparametric and optimal under bimodal histogram distributions.

3. Viola-Jones Integral Image & AdaBoost
II(x,y) = ∑_{x'≤x, y'≤y} i(x', y')

Constant Time Evaluation: Evaluates rectangular Haar features in O(1) time via: Sum = D - B - C + A.

Attentional cascade topology eliminates >95% of non-face subwindows in early stages with near-zero latency.

4. Spatial Moments & Geometric Centroid
m_{pq} = ∑∑ x^p · y^q · I(x,y)

Centroid Coordinates: (x̄, ȳ) = (m₁₀ / m₀₀, m₀₁ / m₀₀)

Central normalized moments provide scale, translation, and rotational invariance for silhouette and contour characterization.
